title: A content landing runs the contract lint on the articles it changes, so a CODE tag without a pointer cannot reach main
goal: backlog.py land runs .claude/skills/kb-verify/lint.py (or the same checks scoped to the changed articles) before sync --push when the landed range changes a kb root's articles, not only when it changes _tools/, so a lint error a worker's content commit adds stops that landing instead of the next code landing. gates.question: ST-urfa4ntj touches _tools/bl_land.py (rule-guarding). When a landing's range changes a kb root's articles and not _tools/, what does land run before sync --push? (a) lint.py on the changed articles' paths only (fast; checks what the landing adds); (b) the whole lint.py (catches what the landing breaks elsewhere, costs a full lint per content landing); (c) the whole LAND_HEAVY pair (rag.py eval and lint.py). And its proof: a planted content landing in test_land_e2e.py whose pointerless CODE tag stops land at step lint, within the ceiling (the plan's choice), replacing the text probe.
